tagline: Hairpins up from Lake Tahoe, hairpins down to Reno.
intro: Out of Incline Village on the north shore of Lake Tahoe, Route 431 climbs the Carson Range by hairpin curves. Partway up, a view area sets out markers pointing to the Sierra peaks around the lake. The top is Mount Rose Summit at 8,911 feet, which the state highway department has called the highest Sierra pass open all year.
Then more hairpins down the east side, past the ski area and overlooks of Reno and Washoe Valley, to Galena on the edge of Reno. Around 1950 this was a dirt road a car could manage only in summer.

moments.title: Incline Village
moments.text: The town is named for a logging incline railway that hauled Tahoe timber 1,400 feet up the mountain, bound for the mines of the Comstock Lode.

moments.title: Mount Rose Summit
moments.text: The road tops out in the saddle between Slide Mountain and Tamarack Peak, where a parking lot and a small building make a highway stop.

moments.title: Mount Rose Ski Tahoe
moments.text: The ski area named for Mount Rose sits on Slide Mountain, across the highway from it, and started out in 1953 as the Reno Ski Bowl.
